name: Startups
title: Product analytics for startups, free up to 10k events
description: Funnels, retention and cohorts for small teams. Free up to 10,000 events a month, then stepped pricing from EUR 10. Cookieless, event data stored in Germany.
tagline: Funnels, retention and cohorts without an enterprise contract or a data team.
intro: Privytics gives a small team the product analytics needed to answer two questions: are new users activating, and are they coming back. You get funnels, retention, cohorts, dashboards, user profiles and custom events, with 10,000 events a month free and no credit card. Event data is stored in Germany and the tracker is cookieless by default, so the setup does not start with a consent management project.

why.title: The price is known before you have revenue
why.body: The steps are published: free up to 10,000 events a month, then EUR 10 for 100k, 20 for 500k, 40 for 1M, 100 for 5M, 200 for 10M, and a custom quote above that. Pricing is driven by event volume, so a launch that goes well moves you one step up a list you already read, not into a sales call. Free is a real tier with one project and 12 months of retention, not a 14 day trial.

why.title: Enough depth for activation and retention, without a data pipeline
why.body: Funnels, retention curves, cohorts and user profiles cover the questions a pre product-market-fit team actually asks: where signup drops off, whether week two retention moved after a change, how one cohort behaves against another. None of it needs a warehouse, a transformation layer or an analytics engineer. If your question is closer to 'what is our week four retention by signup source' than 'run this multi-touch attribution model', this is the right size of tool.

why.title: EU hosting is set up once, at the point where it is cheapest to do
why.body: Event data is stored in Germany, the tracker sets no cookies and writes nothing to the device, and the anonymous visitor id resets every day. Deciding this at ten users costs an afternoon. Deciding it at your first enterprise security review, after two years of events sit somewhere else, costs a migration. You remain the data controller for whatever you send us, including any user id you pass to identify().

why.title: Where another tool is the better call
why.body: Mixpanel, Amplitude and PostHog are stronger at serious analytical depth. If you need advanced behavioural segmentation, experimentation and feature flags in the same tool, a large library of warehouse and CRM integrations, or a mature SQL layer over raw events, pick one of those. Privytics is a newer service than those three, which have been operating for years, and support on the free tier is community only. Weigh that against the published pricing and EU hosting.

steps.title: Add the tracker to your app
steps.body: Paste both tags into the <head> of your pages and replace YOUR_CLIENT_ID with the client id from your Privytics project. Setting apiUrl is required: without it the SDK sends events to OpenPanel's own hosted API instead of yours. If you build with a bundler, npm install @openpanel/web and pass the same options to the OpenPanel constructor instead.

steps.title: Define a small event taxonomy and stick to it
steps.body: Start with the handful of events that make up your activation path, not everything a user can click. Use snake_case verbs in the past tense, keep the event name stable and put the variable parts in properties. Six well-named events you can build a funnel from beat sixty you cannot remember the meaning of. Add the rest once these are answering questions.

steps.title: Identify signed-in users so retention and cohorts follow the person
steps.body: Anonymous tracking is enough for funnels inside one session. To see whether a user came back next week, or to build a cohort from people who signed up in March, pass your own user id as profileId after login. This is opt-in and you need your own lawful basis for it. Call clear() on logout so later events are not attributed to that profile.

faq.q: What analytics tool should an early-stage startup use?
faq.a: If the questions are activation, funnel drop-off and retention, almost any product analytics tool will answer them and the deciding factors are cost, setup time and where data lives. Privytics is free up to 10,000 events a month with one project, and the paid steps are published by volume. If you need experimentation, feature flags or deep behavioural segmentation in the same product, Mixpanel, Amplitude or PostHog are stronger choices.

faq.q: Is Privytics a Mixpanel or Amplitude replacement?
faq.a: For core product analytics, funnels, retention, cohorts, dashboards, user profiles and custom events, it covers the same ground. For advanced analysis it does not: those tools go deeper on segmentation, modelling and integrations, and they have years of production history behind them. Privytics is a newer service than they are. The honest pitch is predictable pricing, EU hosting and enough analytics to run a seed-stage product, not feature parity.

faq.q: What happens to the bill when we grow?
faq.a: You move up a published step rather than into a negotiation. Free covers 10,000 events a month, then EUR 10 for 100k, 20 for 500k, 40 for 1M, 100 for 5M and 200 for 10M, with custom pricing above 10M. Paid plans also add session replay and extend event history from 12 months to 5 years.

faq.q: Do we need a cookie banner for this?
faq.a: That decision is yours as the data controller and we cannot make it for you. What we can describe is the design: the default tracker sets no cookies and stores nothing on the device, and the visitor id is a salted hash of IP, user agent and project id that is rotated daily at midnight UTC rather than a stored identifier. If you call identify() with your own user ids, you are processing identifiable data and need your own lawful basis for it.

faq.q: Can we get session replay on the free plan?
faq.a: No. Session replay is on paid plans only and is opt-in per project. When enabled it masks all text and inputs by default, so you review flows rather than reading what a user typed.

omitted: Any customer count, testimonial, logo wall or reliability figure. None of these are claimed anywhere on the page.

Speed and reliability comparisons against Mixpanel, Amplitude, PostHog or Google Analytics. No comparative measurement was made, so no claim appears in either direction beyond the statement that those tools are analytically deeper.

Any suggestion that using Privytics makes a startup GDPR compliant. The copy describes the design (cookieless default, German storage, rotating salted hash) and states plainly that the reader remains the data controller.
A startup discount, YC deal or credits programme. None exists. The free tier and the published steps are the whole offer.
Seat and team-member pricing. The published pricing is event-volume based and nothing is documented about per-seat charges, so the page does not claim unlimited seats or any seat policy.
A session replay code snippet. Replay is real and paid-only, but no complete script-tag configuration example is published, so no snippet was written rather than guessing the option shape.
The REST API, groups, revenue tracking, setGlobalProperties, increment, decrement and alias. All real, but out of scope for a three-step first-week setup page.

trackAttributes in the init snippet. It is a real option shown on the script tag page, but this page's second step is about a deliberate taxonomy written in code, so the markup-driven path was left out to avoid mixing two approaches.
scriptUrl. Not required and not relevant to a plain script tag or a bundled @openpanel/web setup, so it is absent from every snippet. apiUrl is the one URL that must be set.
Salt rotation time is now stated in full: the copy says 'rotates daily at midnight UTC', matching the documented behaviour and the wording used on the other guides.
